title: T-money vs. WOWPASS vs. Discover Seoul Pass: Which Korea Travel Card Should You Get?
html:
If you're planning your first trip to Korea, you've probably seen three names pop up over and over: T-money, WOWPASS, and Discover Seoul Pass. They sound similar, but they do very different jobs. One is a basic transit card almost everyone uses, one turns your cash into a spendable Korean won balance, and one is a discount pass for paid attractions. Here's what each one actually does, what it costs, and which ones (you may need more than one!) are worth getting for your trip.

T-money: the card everyone uses for buses and subways

T-money is Korea's standard rechargeable transit card. You tap it on a pad at subway turnstiles and when boarding buses, and the fare is deducted automatically — no need to figure out ticket machines or exact change every time. It also works on most intercity buses and even some taxis, and you can use it like a tiny prepaid card at convenience stores for small purchases.

  • Cost to get one: a basic plastic card costs about 2,500 KRW (character or designer editions cost more, around 5,000–10,000 KRW). This is a one-time purchase price, not a deposit.
  • Where to buy it: convenience stores (look for CU, GS25, or 7-Eleven signs), subway station ticket machines, and counters at Incheon Airport.
  • How to top up: at a convenience store counter (cash, 1,000–90,000 KRW per top-up) or at a subway ticket machine that has a "Recharge T-money" option in English. As of 2026, many ticket machines across Seoul subway stations also accept foreign Visa/Mastercard for top-ups, though a small service fee applies.
  • Subway base fare: about 1,550 KRW with T-money (cash fares at the machine are usually a bit higher).


Riders inside a Seoul subway car — tap your T-money card at the gate before you get here. Photo: LWY, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Before you fly home, you can get any unused balance refunded at most convenience stores (a small handling fee is deducted), so you don't need to spend it all down to zero.

WOWPASS: turn your cash into a spendable won balance

WOWPASS solves a different problem: how do you get Korean won onto a card without losing money to bad exchange rates or overseas card fees? A WOWPASS is a prepaid card you load with foreign cash (USD, JPY, EUR, and more than a dozen other currencies) at a self-service kiosk, which converts it to Korean won at a rate that's usually much better than an airport currency exchange counter. The same card also has a built-in T-money transit function — but note that your WOWPASS "spending" balance and your T-money "transit" balance are topped up separately, so you'll load each one on its own.

  • Issuance fee: around 5,500–6,000 KRW (cheaper if you reserve it online in advance).
  • Other fees: about 1,000 KRW if you withdraw your balance back out as cash, and 3,000 KRW if you need a replacement card.
  • Where to find kiosks: the arrivals areas of Incheon Airport (Terminals 1 and 2), plus 300+ subway stations, hotels, and tourist areas around the country. Note that the kiosks right inside Incheon Airport don't do cash withdrawals — they're mainly for loading your card.


The arrivals area at Incheon Airport Terminal 1 — this is where most travelers spot their first WOWPASS kiosk. Photo: Arne Müseler, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

WOWPASS is mainly worth it if you'd rather avoid foreign transaction fees on your regular debit/credit card, or you just like having cash converted once and done. If your bank card already has no foreign fees, a plain T-money card plus your regular card may be all you need.

Discover Seoul Pass: a discount pass for paid attractions

Unlike the other two, Discover Seoul Pass isn't about paying for transit or everyday purchases — it's a sightseeing pass that gives you free or discounted entry to dozens of paid attractions in and around Seoul, like Lotte World, N Seoul Tower's observatory, Nami Island, the COEX Aquarium, and hanbok (traditional Korean clothing) rentals. Passes come as time-based options you activate from first use:

  • 24-hour pass: around 49,000 KRW
  • 48-hour pass: around 70,000 KRW
  • 72-hour pass: around 90,000 KRW
  • 120-hour pass: around 130,000 KRW

There's also a cheaper "Pick 3" style pass if you only want entry to a handful of attractions rather than the full pass benefits. Many passes now bundle in extras like a small amount of free eSIM data and a loaded T-money transit credit, so check what's currently included before you buy.


Lotte World, one of the attractions commonly covered by the Discover Seoul Pass. Photo: Kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Do the math before buying: add up the normal entry prices for the specific attractions you actually plan to visit, and compare that total to the pass price. If you're only hitting one or two paid sights, the pass usually isn't worth it — it pays off when you're cramming in several attractions in a short time.

How Koreans actually get around (hint: not with any of these passes)

Here's a useful bit of perspective: most Korean locals don't carry a separate T-money card at all anymore. Many have T-money built directly into their phone (through a mobile payment app) or into their bank card, and they've never heard of WOWPASS or Discover Seoul Pass — those two are aimed squarely at foreign visitors. If you want to travel a little more like a local once you're comfortable with the basics, a physical T-money card is still the easiest option for visitors, since setting up the Korean mobile versions usually needs a Korean phone number or bank account.

So which one should you get?

For almost every traveler, a T-money card is non-negotiable — buy one on day one. From there, add WOWPASS if you want a simple way to convert cash without losing money on exchange rates, and add a Discover Seoul Pass only if your itinerary is packed with several paid attractions it covers. It's completely normal to end your trip having used all three for different things.

Quick comparison: T-money vs. WOWPASS vs. Discover Seoul Pass

Card/Pass Cost What it's for Best for
T-money ~2,500 KRW card + top-ups Bus/subway fares, small purchases Every traveler
WOWPASS ~5,500–6,000 KRW issuance + loaded balance Converting cash to a spendable won balance Travelers who want to avoid FX fees
Discover Seoul Pass 49,000–130,000 KRW by duration Discounted/free entry to paid attractions Attraction-heavy, short itineraries

💬 Not sure which combination fits your trip? Tell me your itinerary in the comments and I'll help you figure out what's worth buying!
meta_description: T-money, WOWPASS, and Discover Seoul Pass compared: what each one costs, how it works, and which Korea travel card (or combo of them) actually fits your trip.
